brief.headline: AEGIS dual render modes (holo / photoreal), GTA-style crew POV into any unit on the battlefield, and a library of 18 real world landmarks placed on 12 destinations.

items.text: AEGIS render modes: one scene graph, two complete looks. HOLO is the tactical projection; REAL is a lit world with sky gradient, distance fog, sun and bounce fill, draped asphalt streets and models in their authored colours. Modes swap material state, never geometry, so toggling is instant and the simulation cannot desync. Every material registers once with a role, so anything added later gets both looks for free. Button, or H.

AEGIS crew POV: during a battle, tap a unit or press [ / ] and the camera flies from the table into that crew's head over 1.15 s. Helmet-cam framing with the table UI cleared, live HP, heading and range to that unit's own target, and a signal-lost hand-back when the crew is killed. Eye height comes from the unit class, so a prone sniper, a tank commander in the hatch and an Apache pilot are all at their real heights. Cycling walks the combined-arms picture: nine presses gives pilot, tank commander, IFV gunner, vehicle commander, gun chief, launcher crew, gunner, sniper, rifleman.

AEGIS landmarks: 18 structures authored in real metres and merged to one geometry each — Golden Gate, Salesforce, Liberty, Empire State, Eiffel, Fuji, Skytree, Elizabeth Tower, Colosseum, Giza, Opera House, Burj Khalifa, Christ the Redeemer, Taj Mahal, Sagrada Família, capitol, plus generic tower and peak fallbacks. Twelve destinations place them at real offsets from the city centre; the landmark the intel panel names is the one wired to the strike and BDA path, and the rest topple too.

AEGIS added a sniper class — prone soldier model, M107 at 1800 m, and a hold flag so the team occupies a hide instead of joining the advance. That makes the sniper seat a genuinely different experience from the rifleman seat, which was the point of adding it.

AEGIS bugs that only showed up once the camera dropped to eye level: the water surface masked its shape with vertex colour, which is free in an additive hologram and an opaque black plane over the whole map in a lit one (alphaMap now); ground cover was square opaque points that filled the screen from a metre away; road and field overlays were flat quads at a fixed height so half the network sank under rises (they drape now); a collapsed building pointed its window texture at the sky (footprint shrinks, rubble mound settles over it); and the satellite inset renders straight to the GL canvas, so a faded rail did not hide it in POV.

AEGIS cinematic reel was timed purely in milliseconds and had started desynchronising — the salvo and both team-ops legs were being refused as system-busy and silently vanishing. It waits on simulation state now, with a ceiling, and gained a photoreal-toggle beat and a crew-POV beat. All six legs verified green.

AEGIS battle sim: BATTLE button deploys two 24-unit combined-arms forces (Abrams, Bradley, Stryker, Humvee, Paladin, HIMARS, Apache, rifle squads) that acquire, close and engage on published effective ranges. Belt-fed weapons fire 6-9 round bursts and pause; rifles are aimed semi-auto. Armour is checked against each weapon's AP value. Faction rings, tracers, muzzle flashes, live force-strength HUD.

AEGIS military models authored in real metres with one conversion, so soldier/Humvee/Abrams proportions are correct by construction. Includes sloped Abrams glacis and 5.3m gun, Bradley TOW box, M109 fume extractor, Stryker 2+2 axle grouping and slat armour, Apache tandem cockpit. Infantry in standing/kneeling/prone with helmet, plate carrier, ruck and rifle. Houses gained gable roofs, doors, window bays and chimneys.

Fixed a latent bug that had been silently deleting model detail project-wide: mergeParts sized its buffers from the INDEXED vertex count before de-indexing, so overflow writes were swallowed and trailing parts vanished. The Stryker and Humvee were losing their entire hulls. Vertex counts roughly doubled after the fix.

AEGIS worldwide: 51 destinations across all 7 regions, each built from real coordinates and a real ETOPO1 elevation grid fetched at build time and baked in, so it still runs air-gapped. Searchable theater console (G) loads any site in ~2s.
